units.zh: 聖穆皇后柴氏
units.en: Empress Shengmu of the Chai clan
units.literal: Empress Shengmu, née Chai

units.zh: 太祖一后三妃。
units.en: Taizu had one empress and three imperial consorts.
units.literal: Taizu had one empress and three consorts.

units.zh: 聖穆皇后柴氏，邢州堯山人也，與太祖同里，遂以歸焉。
units.en: Empress Shengmu of the Chai clan came from Yaoshan in Xing Prefecture. She and Taizu were neighbors, and he married her.
units.literal: Empress Shengmu, née Chai, was a native of Yaoshan in Xingzhou. She and Taizu were from the same neighborhood, and he took her in marriage.

units.zh: 太祖微時，喜飲博任俠，不拘細行，后常諫止之。
units.en: In his early days Taizu loved wine, dice, and swaggering heroics, caring little for small proprieties; his wife often urged him to stop.
units.literal: When Taizu was still obscure, he delighted in drinking, gambling, and chivalric adventure, heedless of petty conduct; the lady often admonished and restrained him.

units.zh: 太祖狀貌奇偉，后心知其貴人也，事之甚謹。
units.en: Taizu's stature was striking and grand; his wife sensed in her heart that he was destined for greatness and treated him with scrupulous respect.
units.literal: Taizu's bearing was singular and imposing; in her heart the lady knew he was a man of eminence and served him with great deference.

units.zh: 及太祖即位，后已先卒，乃下詔：「故夫人柴氏，追冊為皇后，謚曰聖穆。」
units.en: By the time Taizu ascended the throne, she had already died. He then decreed: "The late Lady Chai is posthumously installed as empress, with the posthumous title Shengmu."
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, the lady had already died beforehand. He thereupon issued an edict: "The late Lady Chai is posthumously enfeoffed as empress, with the posthumous title Shengmu."

units.zh: 淑妃楊氏
units.en: Imperial Consort Shu of the Yang clan
units.literal: Imperial Consort Shu, née Yang

units.zh: 淑妃楊氏，鎮州真定人也。
units.en: Imperial Consort Shu of the Yang clan was from Zhending in Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: Imperial Consort Shu, née Yang, was a native of Zhending in Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 父弘裕，真定少尹。
units.en: Her father Hongyu served as vice prefect of Zhending.
units.literal: Her father Hongyu was Vice-Governor of Zhending.

units.zh: 妃幼以色選入趙王宮，事王熔。
units.en: As a girl she was selected for her looks and sent into the Zhao princely household to serve Wang Rong.
units.literal: While young the consort was chosen for her beauty and entered the palace of the Prince of Zhao, attending Wang Rong.

units.zh: 熔為張文禮所殺，鎮州亂，妃亦流寓民間，後嫁里人石光輔。
units.en: When Rong was killed by Zhang Wenli and Zhen Prefecture was thrown into chaos, she too was cast adrift among the people and later married a local man, Shi Guangfu.
units.literal: Rong was killed by Zhang Wenli; Zhenzhou fell into turmoil, and the consort too wandered among the common people, later marrying a townsman named Shi Guangfu.

units.zh: 居數年，光輔死。
units.en: Several years later Guangfu died.
units.literal: After several years Guangfu died.

units.zh: 太祖柴夫人卒，聞妃有色而賢，遂娶之為繼室。
units.en: After Taizu's wife from the Chai clan died, he heard that this consort was both lovely and worthy and took her as his next wife.
units.literal: When Taizu's Lady Chai died, hearing that the consort was beautiful and virtuous, he took her as his successor wife.

units.zh: 太祖方事漢高祖於太原，天福中妃卒，遂葬太原之近郊。
units.en: Taizu was then in Gaozu of Later Han's service at Taiyuan. She died during the Tianfu reign period and was buried in the outskirts near the city.
units.literal: Taizu was then serving Gaozu of Han at Taiyuan; in the Tianfu era the consort died and was buried in the suburbs near Taiyuan.

units.zh: 太祖即位，廣順元年九月，追冊為淑妃。
units.en: After Taizu became emperor, in the ninth month of Guangshun 1 she was posthumously installed as Imperial Consort Shu.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne, in the ninth month of the first year of Guangshun she was posthumously enfeoffed as Imperial Consort Shu.

units.zh: 拜妃弟廷璋為右飛龍使，廷璋辭曰：「臣父老矣，願以授之。」
units.en: He appointed the consort's younger brother Tingzhang as Right Commissioner of the Soaring Dragon. Tingzhang declined: "My father is elderly; I would rather the appointment go to him."
units.literal: He appointed the consort's younger brother Tingzhang as Right Commissioner of the Soaring Dragon; Tingzhang declined, saying, "My father is old; I wish the post to be given to him."

units.zh: 太祖曰：「吾方思之，豈忘爾父邪！」
units.en: Taizu replied, "I was just thinking of that—how could I forget your father!"
units.literal: Taizu said, "I was just thinking of that—how could I forget your father!"

units.zh: 即召弘裕，弘裕老不能行，乃就其家拜金紫光祿大夫、真定少尹。
units.en: He immediately summoned Hongyu. Too frail to travel, Hongyu received at home the titles Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and vice prefect of Zhending.
units.literal: He at once summoned Hongyu. Hongyu was too old to travel, so at his home he was invested as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and as Vice-Governor of Zhending.

units.zh: 太祖崩，葬嵩陵，一后三妃皆當陪葬，而太原未克，世宗詔有司營嵩陵之側為虛墓以俟。
units.en: When Taizu died he was interred at Song Mausoleum. The empress and three consorts were all to be buried with him, but Taiyuan had not yet fallen, so Shizong ordered officials to prepare vacant tombs beside the mausoleum until the time came.
units.literal: When Taizu died he was buried at Songling; the one empress and three consorts were all to be buried with him, but Taiyuan had not yet been taken. Shizong ordered the officials to prepare empty tombs beside Songling to await them.

units.zh: 顯德元年，世宗已敗劉旻於高平，遂攻太原，太原閉壁被圍，乃遷妃喪而葬之。
units.en: In Xiande 1, after Shizong had defeated Liu Chong at Gaoping, he marched on Taiyuan. With the city shut up under siege, he had the consort's remains brought forward and buried.
units.literal: In the first year of Xiande, Shizong having already defeated Liu Chong at Gaoping, then attacked Taiyuan. Taiyuan shut its walls and was besieged, whereupon he moved the consort's coffin and buried her.

units.zh: 貴妃張氏
units.en: Imperial Consort Gui of the Zhang clan
units.literal: Imperial Consort Gui, née Zhang

units.zh: 貴妃張氏，鎮州真定人也。
units.en: Imperial Consort Gui of the Zhang clan was from Zhending in Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: Imperial Consort Gui, née Zhang, was a native of Zhending in Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 祖記，成德軍節度判官、檢校兵部尚書。
units.en: Her grandfather Ji had been adjutant of the Chengde military commission and acting Minister of War.
units.literal: Her grandfather Ji was military adjutant of the Chengde command and Acting Minister of War.

units.zh: 父同芝，事趙王王熔為諮呈官，官至檢校工部尚書。
units.en: Her father Tongzhi had served Wang Rong of Zhao as memorial presenter and reached the post of acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: Her father Tongzhi served Prince of Zhao Wang Rong as memorial presenter and rose to Acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 熔死，鎮州亂，莊宗遣幽州符存審以兵討張文禮，裨將武從諫館於妃家，見妃尚幼，憐之，而從諫家在太原，遂以妃歸，為其子婦。
units.en: After Rong's death threw Zhen Prefecture into chaos, Zhuangzong sent Fu Cunjian from Youzhou against Zhang Wenli. The subordinate commander Wu Congjian was quartered at her family's house, took pity on the girl still in her youth, and—his own family being in Taiyuan—brought her home as a daughter-in-law.
units.literal: When Rong died Zhenzhou was in turmoil. Zhuangzong sent Fu Cunjian of Youzhou with troops to punish Zhang Wenli. The lieutenant Wu Congjian lodged at the consort's family home, saw that she was still young, and pitied her. Congjian's family was in Taiyuan, so he took the consort back and made her his son's wife.

units.zh: 久之，太祖事漢高祖於太原，楊夫人卒，而武氏子亦卒，乃納妃為繼室。
units.en: Years later, while Taizu was in Gaozu of Later Han's service at Taiyuan, Lady Yang died and Wu's son died as well; Taizu then took the consort as his next wife.
units.literal: After a long while Taizu was serving Gaozu of Han at Taiyuan; Lady Yang died, and Wu's son also died, whereupon he took the consort as successor wife.

units.zh: 太祖貴，累封吳國夫人。
units.en: As Taizu rose in stature she was repeatedly promoted, eventually to Lady of Wu.
units.literal: When Taizu rose in rank she was repeatedly enfeoffed as Lady of the State of Wu.

units.zh: 太祖以兵入京師，漢遣劉銖戮其家，妃與諸子皆死。
units.en: When Taizu marched into the capital with his army, Later Han sent Liu Zhu to massacre his household; the consort and all his sons were killed.
units.literal: When Taizu entered the capital with troops, Han sent Liu Zhu to slaughter his household; the consort and all his sons perished.

units.zh: 太祖即位，追冊為貴妃。
units.en: After Taizu became emperor he posthumously installed her as Imperial Consort Gui.
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne he posthumously enfeoffed her as Imperial Consort Gui.

units.zh: 德妃董氏
units.en: Imperial Consort De of the Dong clan
units.literal: Imperial Consort De, née Dong

units.zh: 〈（太祖子侗信侄守願奉超遜）〉
units.en: (Taizu's sons Tong and Xin; nephews Shouyuan, Fengchao, and Xun)〉
units.literal: (Taizu's sons Tong and Xin; nephews Shouyuan, Fengchao, and Xun)〉

units.zh: 德妃董氏，鎮州靈壽人也。
units.en: Imperial Consort De of the Dong clan was from Lingshou in Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: Imperial Consort De, née Dong, was a native of Lingshou in Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 祖文廣，唐深州錄事參軍。
units.en: Her grandfather Wenguang had been recording secretary of Shen Prefecture under Tang.
units.literal: Her grandfather Wenguang was recording secretary of Shen Prefecture under Tang.

units.zh: 父光嗣，趙州昭慶尉。
units.en: Her father Guangsi served as magistrate of Zhaoqing in Zhao Prefecture.
units.literal: Her father Guangsi was magistrate of Zhaoqing in Zhao Prefecture.

units.zh: 妃幼穎悟，始能言，聞樂聲知其律呂。
units.en: From childhood she was exceptionally bright: as soon as she could talk, she could tell pitch and mode whenever she heard music.
units.literal: The consort was clever from childhood; as soon as she could speak, upon hearing music she knew its pitch and mode.

units.zh: 年七歲，鎮州亂，其家失之，為潞州牙將所得，置諸褚中以歸。
units.en: At seven, during the chaos in Zhen Prefecture, her family lost track of her. A Luzhou garrison officer seized her, tucked her into a sack, and took her away.
units.literal: At age seven, when Zhenzhou was in turmoil, her family lost her; a garrison officer of Luzhou obtained her, put her in a bag, and carried her off.

units.zh: 潞將妻嘗生女，輒不育，得妃憐之，養以為子，過於所生。
units.en: The commander's wife had borne daughters who never lived; when she got the girl she cherished her and raised her as a daughter, loving her even more than her own children.
units.literal: The Luzhou commander's wife had borne daughters who always failed to survive; obtaining the consort she pitied her and raised her as a daughter, loving her more than a child of her own flesh.

units.zh: 居五六年，妃家悲思，其兄瑀求之人間，莫知所在。
units.en: Five or six years passed. Her family mourned and missed her; her elder brother Yu searched the world for her, but no one knew where she was.
units.literal: After five or six years the consort's family grieved and longed for her; her elder brother Yu sought her among the people but did not know where she was.

units.zh: 潞將仕於京師，遇瑀，欣然歸之，時年十三。
units.en: The Luzhou commander was on duty in the capital when he met Yu and gladly gave her back; she was thirteen by then.
units.literal: The Luzhou commander was serving at the capital and met Yu; gladly he returned her—she was then thirteen.

units.zh: 瑀以嫁里人劉進超，進超亦仕晉為內職。
units.en: Yu married her to a local man, Liu Jinchao, who also held an inner-court post under Jin.
units.literal: Yu gave her in marriage to a townsman, Liu Jinchao; Jinchao also served Jin in an inner-office post.

units.zh: 契丹犯闕，進超歿於虜中，妃嫠居洛陽。
units.en: When the Khitans stormed the capital Jinchao died in their hands, and she lived as a widow in Luoyang.
units.literal: When the Khitans violated the capital Jinchao died among the invaders, and the consort lived as a widow in Luoyang.

units.zh: 漢高祖由太原入京師，太祖從，過洛陽，聞妃有賢行，聘之。
units.en: When Gaozu of Later Han entered the capital from Taiyuan, Taizu went with him. Passing through Luoyang he heard of her virtue and took her as his wife.
units.literal: Gaozu of Han entered the capital from Taiyuan; Taizu followed, passed through Luoyang, heard of the consort's worthy conduct, and betrothed her.

units.zh: 太祖建國，中宮虛位，遂冊為德妃。
units.en: When Taizu founded Later Zhou the empress's seat stood empty, and he installed her as Imperial Consort De.
units.literal: When Taizu founded the state the central palace was vacant, and he thereupon installed her as Imperial Consort De.

units.zh: 廣順三年卒，年三十九。
units.en: She died in Guangshun 3, at the age of thirty-nine.
units.literal: She died in the third year of Guangshun, aged thirty-nine.

units.zh: 妃兄三人：瑀官至太子右贊善大夫，玄之、自明皆至刺史。
units.en: She had three brothers: Yu rose to Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace; Xuanzhi and Ziming both became regional inspectors.
units.literal: The consort had three elder brothers: Yu rose to Right Supporter of the Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace; Xuanzhi and Ziming both reached the rank of regional inspector.

units.zh: 初，帝舉兵於魏，漢以兵圍帝第，時張貴妃與諸子青哥、意哥，侄守筠、奉超、定哥，皆被誅。
units.en: Earlier, when the emperor raised his army in Wei, Later Han besieged his residence. Imperial Consort Zhang, the sons Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge were all executed.
units.literal: Earlier, when the Emperor raised troops in Wei, Han surrounded his residence with troops. At that time Imperial Consort Zhang, the sons Qingge and Yige, and the nephews Shoujun, Fengchao, and Dingge were all put to death.

units.zh: 青哥、意哥，不知其母誰氏。
units.en: Who bore Qingge and Yige is not recorded.
units.literal: Qingge and Yige—whose mothers they were is unknown.

units.zh: 太祖即位，詔故第二子青哥贈太尉，賜名侗；
units.en: When Taizu became emperor he decreed that his late second son Qingge be posthumously made Grand Commandant and given the name Tong;
units.literal: When Taizu took the throne he decreed that the late second son Qingge be posthumously granted Grand Commandant and given the name Tong;

units.zh: 第三子意哥贈司空，賜名信；
units.en: that the third son Yige be posthumously made Minister of Works and given the name Xin;
units.literal: the third son Yige be posthumously granted Minister of Works and given the name Xin;

units.zh: 皇侄守筠贈左領軍衛將軍，以筠聲近榮，為世宗避，更名守願；
units.en: that the imperial nephew Shoujun be posthumously made general of the Left Army Guard—because jun sounded like "glory," it was changed for Shizong's taboo to Shouyuan;
units.literal: the imperial nephew Shoujun be posthumously granted General of the Left Army Guard; because jun sounded like glory, to avoid Shizong's taboo he was renamed Shouyuan;

units.zh: 奉超贈左監門衛將軍；
units.en: that Fengchao be posthumously made general of the Left Gate Guard;
units.literal: Fengchao be posthumously granted General of the Left Gate Guard;

units.zh: 定哥贈左千年衛將軍，賜名遜。
units.en: and that Dingge be posthumously made general of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and given the name Xun.
units.literal: Dingge be posthumously granted General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard and given the name Xun.

units.zh: 世宗顯德四年夏四月癸未，詔曰：「禮以緣情，恩以悼往，矧在友於之列，尤鐘惻愴之情。
units.en: On guiwei day in the fourth month of summer, Xiande 4, Shizong issued an edict: "Rites arise from affection, and grace mourns the dead; how much more among brothers, where grief cuts especially deep.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande, on the day guiwei of the fourth month of summer, Shizong issued an edict: "Rites follow affection; grace mourns the departed—how much more among brothers, where heartfelt grief is especially deep.

units.zh: 故皇弟贈太保侗、贈司空信，景邊初啟，大年不登，俾予終鮮，實勤予懷。
units.en: My late brothers, posthumously Grand Guardian Tong and posthumously Minister of Works Xin, when the border war had barely begun did not live out their full span, leaving me brotherless to the end—a sorrow that truly weighs on my heart.
units.literal: The late imperial younger brothers, posthumously Grand Guardian Tong and posthumously Minister of Works Xin, when the frontier campaign had just opened did not reach full years, leaving me without brothers to the end—this truly weighs on my heart.

units.zh: 侗可贈太傅，追封郯王；
units.en: Tong shall be posthumously made Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Prince of Tan;
units.literal: Tong may be posthumously granted Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as Prince of Tan;

units.zh: 信司徒，𣏌王。」
units.en: Xin shall be posthumously made Minister over the Masses and enfeoffed as Prince of Qi."
units.literal: Xin, Minister over the Masses, Prince of Qi."

units.zh: 又詔曰：「故皇從弟贈左領軍衞將軍守愿、贈左監門衞將軍奉超、贈左千牛衞將軍遜等，頃因季世，不享遐齡，每念非辜，難忘有慟。
units.en: He issued another edict: "My late cousins, posthumously General of the Left Army Guard Shouyuan, posthumously General of the Left Gate Guard Fengchao, and posthumously General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard Xun, perished in these troubled times without reaching a full span of years. Whenever I recall their innocence, my grief will not be stilled.
units.literal: He issued another edict: "The late imperial cousins, posthumously General of the Left Army Guard Shouyuan, posthumously General of the Left Gate Guard Fengchao, posthumously General of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard Xun, and others—lately, in a degenerate age, did not enjoy long life. Whenever I think how innocent they were, I cannot forget my grief.

units.zh: 守愿可贈左衞大將軍，奉超右衞大將軍，遜右武衞大將軍。」
units.en: Shouyuan shall be posthumously made Grand General of the Left Guard; Fengchao, Grand General of the Right Guard; and Xun, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard."
units.literal: Shouyuan may be posthumously granted Grand General of the Left Guard; Fengchao, Grand General of the Right Guard; Xun, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard."

candidatePacket.instructions: Review dates, event ownership, conversions, endpoint evidence, age reckoning, omitted life dates, and active-date hints. Read all Chinese units for omissions; English is not independent evidence. Do not re-extract names or mentions. For each item identify whose event is dated and justify each endpoint. Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.

findings.problem: The dated source events are posthumous investitures, reburial, or later commemoration, but their dates are presented as active-date attestations for people already described as dead.
findings.action: Remove the misleading personal active dates and hints; retain each dated reception only as a separately classified posthumous event tied to its own actor and source unit.

findings.problem: The text places an event somewhere during Tianfu or in a relative sequence, not throughout the complete AD 936–944 era interval.
findings.action: Remove the unsupported full-era intervals and active-date hints; retain the Chinese temporal wording without a fabricated Western start and end.

findings.problem: The narrative reports the Zhenzhou aftermath and a Later Tang response but does not evidence that every named person was active throughout the supplied AD 923–926 or AD 900–926 spans.
findings.action: Replace the full activity intervals and hints with undated source context unless a separately cited, person-specific event date is supplied.

findings.problem: The chapter says that Taizu raised troops and the Later Han forces executed household members; it gives no source basis for the AD 950–951 two-year activity interval.
findings.action: Remove the unsupported two-year ranges and hints. Preserve the execution and later memorial facts with their exact Chinese relative wording.

findings.problem: The ages of seven and thirteen and the phrase Zhenzhou chaos do not by themselves establish the imported Western interval or exact AD 927 return year.
findings.action: Remove the inferred Western years while preserving the stated sui ages and the undated sequence; do not calculate a birth or event year from inclusive-age data without independent evidence.

findings.problem: Generic dynasty, family-office, and later-summary references are expanded into broad personal activity spans not stated in the chapter.
findings.action: Remove these unsupported date intervals and active hints while retaining the undated offices and kinship references.

findings.problem: Serving Jin and dying during the Khitan incursion are source-relative statements; they do not show service across all AD 936–947 or a two-year death interval.
findings.action: Remove the full-period intervals and active hint; preserve the undated service and death-in-invaders claim with Chinese source context.
